title: CIP: Improve CRC Checks
description:
- Concurrent Connections: Add CRC validation
- Safety: CRC-S5: 3-250 Byte Extended Format: Use the actual complemented data bytes
  - Do not calculate the complement, because the calculation needs the packet data
- Minor cleanup: reduce variable scope

notes.body: I think this belongs in wsutil/crc32.c

The items in wsutil/crc32.c seem to be more generic. This CRC polynomial/algorithm is only used by CIP (from what I could see)

Does it still make sense to put it in crc32.c, if this won't be generically used by other protocols?

Not sure why the check didn't log output ([`Commit Check:`](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/.gitlab-ci.yml#L686)) :
> `        MESSAGE="ℹ️ This merge request has more than one commit. Please squash any trivial ones:`  
  
Someone will come along and ask if you can squash your commits.  
  
From the job log:  
```
running mr note deduplication: GET https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/wireshark/wireshark/merge_requests/17391/notes: 401 {message: 401 Unauthorized}
ℹ️ This merge request has more than one commit. Please squash any trivial ones:
  ~~~
  71ba69f4 Concurrent Connections: Add CRC validation
9d276826 Safety: CRC-S5: 3-250 Byte Extended Format: Use the actual complemented data bytes
ff4fe9b2 Minor cleanup: reduce variable scope
  ~~~
```  
  
Squash example on wiki: https://wiki.wireshark.org/Development/SubmittingPatches#quickstart
'Squash commits when merge request is accepted' should already be checked for this MR. The 3 commits are distinct pieces
I think there are occasional issues where that doesn't work so recommendation is to squash ahead of time.

I think those are for "trivial" commits, eg: whitespace, review fixes, lint fixes, etc.

The 3x commits here were separate, distinct changes

Sorry for the confusion. Sometimes it seems to be iterative process where a MR is close to being approved but only after the squash. And now I learn there are cases where better to leave them separate. :-)
It's easier with one commit per MR.

@AndersBroman Did you mean before or after gitlab does the autosquash? With autosquash, everything going to master will just be 1 commit

I can do whatever you guys prefer in the future. But, I think having separate commits helps when there are different changes going in. eg:
- Separate out refactor commits from the real change, so it's easier to see the difference when reviewing, instead of everything mixed up
- If you don't like something in a MR, then I can drop 1x commit, and leave the others in place. With 1 commit, it's a lot of extra manual work during review, to pull those changes out

Thanks for merging either way :)

If I understood correctly the auto squash might produce a bad commit message. One MR one commit no problem :-)
Easy peacy.

+static uint32_t compute_crc_cc(const uint8_t* pData, size_t size)
+{
+   uint32_t crc = 0xFFFFFFFF;
+   for (; size > 0; --size)
+   {
+      crc = crc32_cc_table[*pData++ ^ (uint8_t)crc] ^ (crc >> 8);
+   }
+   return crc;
+}
